source.title: RepSelect: Robust LLM Unlearning via Representation Selectivity
source.authors: Filip Sondej; Yu-Shi Yang; Adam Mahdi

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present. Some figure and table layouts are flattened, but the results used below are stated in text or tables.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests relearning and few-shot attacks and reports that its new method, RepSelect, resists them better than several baselines, qualifying the claim that unlearning is generally shallow and easily reversed.
record.gate_note: The study reports numerical results for fine-tuning, few-shot, and adaptive attacks, as well as general-capability checks. Figure-only results without readable values, including individual cells of the main fine-tuning comparison and several ablations, are not transcribed as numerical rows. The paper's discussion of other studies' results is not recorded as this study's evidence.
record.test_reason: The study runs fine-tuning, few-shot (k=5,10) and adaptive relearning attacks on five baselines (including RMU, from WMDP) and on its new method RepSelect. It reports baselines being reverted, and RepSelect resisting most attacks at matched WikiText KL. The results bear on B, E and F, and on A's capability-preservation part, and argue that shallowness is not inherent to unlearning.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Add that the authors also report existing baselines as shallow: fine-tuning and few-shot examples bring the behaviour back. They conclude robust post-hoc unlearning is achievable, and that an SVD-aware adaptive attacker gains nothing over standard fine-tuning.
record.recipe_differences: RepSelect is a new method: it uses SVD-based collapse of high-variance components of forget-set weight gradients, with LoRA elicitation, and compares against GradDiff, NPO, SimNPO, RMU, and UNDIAL. It is not a reproduction of the original sources' methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome depends on method, model, benchmark, and attack type. Removing LoRA costs 14–66% of unlearning gain on RWKU, Sycophancy, and Animal Abuse but is neutral on WMDP benchmarks. Few-shot and adaptive attacks cover only two models and two benchmarks. The paper also reports that SVD source can vary by target type: forget-set SVD tends to work better for knowledge, retain-set SVD for tendencies.

fits_no_version.finding: Baselines and a fine-tuning attacker place 33–41% (Llama) and 50–62% (Qwen) of weight-update norm in the top-50 forget PCs, against ~4–6% for RepSelect. Top PCs are shared with retain data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shallow unlearning edits a high-variance subspace shared with benign data, the same subspace a fine-tuning attacker recovers.

fits_no_version.finding: An unlearning gradient for one fact transfers ~50% to translations with similar surface tokens and weakly to Russian/Portuguese (Llama-3.2-1B, gradient cosine only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning updates may be language-specific, leaving cross-lingual access (related to E).

record.problems: The few-shot and adaptive evaluations cover only two models and two benchmarks; the authors say compute limits restricted coverage. Several individual main fine-tuning results are shown in figures rather than readable numeric tables in the supplied text. Results are tuned with Optuna on the reported attack metric, and the authors note that reporting the mean of the 10 best trials out of 30 is optimistic, though they also provide median-trial results. The adaptive attack is weaker than standard fine-tuning in the reported settings.
record.rows_left_out: Individual result values from Figure 6, Figure 7, Figures 8–10, and Figures 15–16 were not extracted where the supplied text presents them only as plots without readable numerical values. Additional k=10 comparator scores and no-attack scores from Table 7, and baseline adaptive-attack values from Table 10, were omitted to stay within the row limit and prioritize RepSelect, k=5 comparisons, and attack outcomes. The paper's representation-update norm analyses (Figures 4 and 13; Tables 11, 19, and 20) were not recorded as direct tests of recovery by internal edits.

untested.parts: Near-chance accuracy is not measured; the study uses answer/harmful-response probability. Jailbreak, rephrasing, language and quantization attacks are not run.
Relearning on unrelated or loosely related data is not a separate condition. The relearn set is held-out same-domain data (half the WMDP questions, or disjoint BeaverTails pairs).
No direction ablation and no test of blocking versus deletion. Only weight-update subspace analysis is reported (see fits_no_version).
Only few-shot demonstrations from the relearn split are tested. Rephrasing, jailbreaks (said not to apply) and other languages are not tested.
RepSelect's resistance to quantization, jailbreaks, rephrasing and other languages is untested. Few-shot and adaptive attacks cover only 2 models × 2 datasets.

missing.what: Baselines (NPO, RMU) on Animal Abuse are almost fully reverted by relearning, even after one epoch. NPO and RMU barely unlearn WMDP-Bio within the KL budget.
Per-method no-attack scores from Table 7, needed as the pre-attack baseline for every few-shot row. Also k=10 baseline scores.
Baseline adaptive-attack results: all methods rise only ~0.001–0.019, the same as no-unlearn.
Animal Abuse post-attack RepSelect only ~13% relative per-token reduction; median-trial baselines barely unlearn.

record.verdict_notes: The two attack tables use different metrics: Tables 2/7 Bio is accuracy at temperature 1, Tables 3/10 is recall probability. Few-shot models came from a separate 5-trial search, so their pre-attack scores differ from the Table 3 models. On Qwen Bio several baselines (GradDiff, SimNPO, RMU) did not unlearn at all, so their few-shot rows can't show recovery. The no-unlearn post-FT values appear only in Figure 6. Comparisons are at a WikiText KL ≤ 0.01 budget, with means of the top 10 of 30 Optuna trials.

versions.untested_parts: Near-chance behavior and general-capability preservation are reported for RepSelect, but not established uniformly for every baseline or every benchmark. Jailbreaks, rephrasing, other languages, and quantization are not tested.
Fine-tuning is tested using relearn sets related to the target data. The study does not test relearning from unrelated examples or only a subset of forgotten facts as separate attack conditions.

No experiment ablates an activation direction to restore the target behavior, and the study does not test whether the target knowledge remains accessible through a distinct access-blocking mechanism rather than being removed.
Few-shot prompting with target-related demonstrations is tested. Prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, and in-context information unrelated to the target are not tested.
RepSelect is evaluated against fine-tuning, few-shot, and an adaptive fine-tuning attack. Resistance to quantization, prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, or other-language prompts is not tested.
